Kṛśānusaṃhitā

Kṛśāśva

Kṛṣipaddhati
or kR. pArAzara or kR. vidhAnapaddhati agriculture. in 243 verses. attributed to Parāśara. Cambr. 25. Cuttack 15 (Kṛ. [Page284-b] vidhānapaddhati). Dacca 4558. IO. 3168. 6475. K. 172. L. 317. Mandlik p. 59, BG. 38 (copy of a Calcutta ms.). SSPC. I. I. 310.
Pt.. (1) Calcutta, 1915. Vangavasi edn. with Bengali transl. (2) using three of the above mss., Bib. Ind. 285. 1960, with English transl., by G. P. Majumdar an. S. C. Banerji.
See also ABORI. XXXVI. i-ii. 1955, p.. 1-32.

Kṛṣiśāsana
in verse, in 11 chs., compiled by Daśarathaśāstrin, son of Ṛṣi Nārāyaṇa.
Pt.. with C. Nārāyaṇabhāṣya by same in Skt. an. a Hindi C. Nagpur, 1920. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 238 an. IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938, p. 1365.

Kṛṣiśāstra
on times propitions for different agricultural an. allied operations. MT. 5276 (inc.) (in Anuṣṭubhs).
Pt.. in App. a. the end of the Bib. Ind. edn. (1960) of Kṛṣipārāśara noted above.
--by Kāśyapa. Adyar.

Kṛṣṇa

Kṛṣṇa
father of king Indrāyudha of Kanauj, patron of Jinasena II, a. of Harivaṁśapurāṇa. Jain. written in 783 A. D. [Page285-a.
See NCC. II. p. 257b where the description of Indrāyudha a. Rāṣṭrakūṭa king should be corrected.

Kṛṣṇa
son of Sajjana of Prāgvāṭa family; patron of Śrīcandra Muni (a. of Kathākośa); an. adviser of king Mūlarāja of Anhilwad.
See NCC. III. p. 131b.

Kṛṣṇa
king praised by Bhānudatta (a. of Rasamañjarī etc.) in two verses of his Rasapārijāta; also q. in Padyaracanā (p. 16, verse 2 an. p. 27, verse 63). Identity not certain.
See Kane, His.. of Skt. Poetics p. 297 fn.

Kṛṣṇa

Kṛṣṇa

Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta
stotra on Kṛṣṇa by Kṛṣṇalīlāśuka or Līlāśuka or Bilvamaṅgala, son of Dāmodara an. Nīlī an. pupil of Īśānadeva (cf. end of 1st śataka) an. of Somagiri (cf. opening verse).
In most mss., found in three śatakas called Āśvāsas (about 300 verses in all); a. against the S. Indian tradition, inclusive of mss., an. the C.s, taking the stotra a. comprising the three centuries, the Bengal tradition, going to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya who secured a ms. of the first śataka only during his S. Indian tour, has taken the stotra a. consisting of the first śataka only, the C.s written there being only on the first śataka.
Verses in KK. are also found in other Kṛṣṇa-stotras of Bilvamaṅgala like Kṛṣṇabālacarita, Bālagopālastuti an. Bilvamaṅgalastotra.
For a discussion of this textual problem, see S. K. D., critical edn. of the text, 1st śataka only, Intro., Dacca Uni. Ori. Pub. Ser. 5, 1938; D., ABORI. XVII. i. p.. 173-188 an. IHQ. XX. p.. 179-181; H. G. Narahari, Adyar Library Bulletin VIII. p.. 37-46; BDCRI. 1955-6, p.. 42-45. [Page295-b] For a summary of the discussions an. evidences in favour of the S. Indian tradition, see K. Kunjunni Raja, Contribution of Kerala to Skt. Lit. p.. 34-40.

Kṛṣṇalīlāśuka,_līlāśuka
or bi(v.)lvamaGgala saint, philosopher an. scholar, son of Nīlī an. Dāmodara an. disciple of Īśānadeva (see verse a. end of first Śataka of Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta). Durgāprasāda Yati, in his C. on Śrīcihnakāvya mentions him a. pupil or belonging to the line of pupils of Padmapādamuni, from which some take him to have belonged to the Tekkemaṭham a. Trichur, said to have been founded by Padmapāda. In the opening verse of Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta occur two other names a. Gurus, Cintāmaṇi an. Somagiri. [Page355-a. Bilva(Villu)maṅgala (given sometimes a. Kodaṇḍamaṅgala) seems to be his house-name. For discussion about the life, date an. works of different Kṛṣṇalīlāśuka-Bilvamaṅgalas an. the question of their identity or otherwise see Ullur S. Paramesvara Iyer, Proceed. AIOC. IX. Trivandrum, 1937, p.. 471-91; S. K. D., Intro. to his edn. of Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta; D.. K. K. Raja, Contribution of Kerala to Skt. Lit. p.. 31-51. Ref. to a. Karṇāmṛtakavi by Gaṅgādevī, consort of Vīrakampana (1343-79 A. D.), in Madhurāvijaya I. 12.
Works ascribed to him fall into three classes: (i) a few Advaitic, Śaiva an. Śākta hymns an. commentary, referring to his original or basic faith (ref. to also in Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta II. 21 zaivA vayaM etc.); (ii) ecstatic hymns on Kṛṣṇa a. the Divine Baby, together with hymns on Rāma an. Nṛsiṁha; an. (iii) works on Skt. an. Pkt. grammar, inclusive of illustrative poems of this class.
In the second class, there is much overlapping, verses in smaller collections found in larger ones an. so on.
In some stotra-mss., a stotra of his is described a. brother of Stotra-ratna (Stotraratna-sodara, see MT. 4320, Bṛndāvanastotra an. Abhinavakaustubhamālā in TSS. 211, first work), from which we may suppose that there is another hymn of his not listed below, called Stotraratna.

Kṛṣṇaśeṣa
or zeSa kRSNa of the celebrated Śeṣa family of Benaras; grandson of Śeṣa Rāmacandra, son of Śeṣa Nṛsiṁha (a. of Govindārṇava, dh.), elder brother of Śeṣa Cintāmaṇi (a. of Rasamañjarī- [Page365-a. vyākhyā); father of Śeṣa Vīreśvara (guru of Jagannātha Paṇḍitarāja) an. Śeṣa Nārāyaṇa (a. of Mahābhāṣyavyākhyā-Sūktiratnākara).
Latter half of the 16th Cent. A. D.
Was patronised by:
1. Narottama of Tāṇḍavapura near Benares, the youngest brother of Govindacandra who prompted Kṛṣṇa's father Nṛsiṁha to compile the Govindārṇava. Narottama prompted Śeṣa Kṛṣṇa to write the Pārijātaharaṇacampū an. the Padacandrikā.
2. Govardhanadhārin or Giridhārin, son of Akbar's minister, Toḍara Malla; prompted Śeṣa Kṛṣṇa to write the drama Kaṁsavadha.
3. Pilājī, son of Keśavadāsa who showed his prowess in the South an. is styled ‘Paramavaiṣṇava’ prompted Śeṣa Kṛṣṇa to write the Śūdrācāraśiromaṇi. The BORI. ms. 50 of 1872-73 of this work is dated 4th March 1591.
4. Vīravara of Patrapuñja, in the territory between the Ganges an. the Jumna, prompted Śeṣa Kṛṣṇa to write the Prakriyākaumudīprakāśa for the education of his son Kalyāṇa.
Śeṣa Kṛṣṇa's contemporaries in Benares: Bhāvā Gaṇeśa Dīkṣita (of the Cittapāvanas); Gopī Bhaṭṭa (of the Gūrjaras); Vidyānivāsa Bhaṭṭācārya (father of Viśvanāthapañcānana) (of the Gauḍas); Raghupati Upādhyāya (of the Tairabhuktas). Śeṣa Kṛṣṇa was the chief of the Mahārāṣṭra Paṇḍits.
See also Ind. Ant. 41. p.. 248-251.

Kṛṣṇopaniṣad
mainly in a recension represented by most of the mss. in which except for a few initial prose passages the text is in verses; N. S. Press edn. of 120 Up.. (1948) (p.. 599-601) corresponds to this an. Upaniṣad Brahmendra's C. is on this text. In a few [Page028-a. mss., IO. 491 (19) an. L. 109, the initial prose is partly omitted an. partly put in verses; Nārāyaṇa's Dīpikā is on this text. Adyar Up. p. 164 represents the same text but with a different set of verses in the beg. an. a closing prose passage; this is also in two khaṇḍas instead of one an. Schrader designates this a. the Southern. Appayācārya's C. is probably on this.
The name Kṛṣṇatāpanī or Kṛṣṇottaratāpanī refers not to this Up., but to the Gopālatāpanī an. G. uttaratāpanī. See RASB. II. 1730. (211A) an. p. 3, Intro. of Jacob, to his Eleven Ātharvaṇa Up.., p. 3.
